courses.description: Study of the standard solo literature including solo excerpts from larger works, i.e., cantata, oratorio, and opera. Supplements the student's knowledge of the literature in his/her major field. 1 undergraduate hour. 1 graduate hour.
courses.prereqText: Junior standing in voice, or consent of instructor and concurrent registration in MUS 481.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Vocal Repertoire II
courses.description: Continuation of the study of the standard solo literature including solo excerpts from larger works, i.e., cantata, oratorio, and opera. Supplements the student's knowledge of the literature in his/her major field. 1 undergraduate hour. 1 graduate hour.
courses.prereqText: Junior standing in voice, or consent of instructor and concurrent registration in MUSC 405.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Proseminar in Music
courses.description: Special preparation in specialized fields of musicology, composition-theory, performance, and music education. 0 to 4 undergraduate hours. 0 to 4 graduate hours. Approved for Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated to a maximum of 16 hours.
courses.prereqText: Senior or graduate standing in music or music education; consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Artist Diploma Recital
courses.description: Recital presented in partial fulfillment of requirements for the Artist Diploma. Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated in the same term to a maximum of 2 hours. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 4 hours.
courses.prereqText: Admission to the Artist Diploma program on the basis of an audition.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Grad Music History Review
courses.description: Review of Western music history both before 1750 ( MUS 501 section A) and after 1750 ( MUS 501 section B). Refreshes knowledge and understanding of representative examples of repertoire as well as the historical context in which music was written. May be repeated up to 8 hours in separate terms.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Graduate Theory Review
courses.description: Review of concepts from undergraduate music theory, including materials from the common practice period (50xA) and the twentieth century (50xB). Concepts studied include compositional materials and basic form and analysis. May be repeated. Credit is not given towards graduate degrees.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate standing in music.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Grad. Jazz Improv. I
courses.description: Practical application of mid- to upper level melodic, harmonic, and rhythmic principles used in jazz improvisation. Practice in the use of jazz chord qualities, upper extensions, and upper altered extensions used in jazz. Descriptions of mid-level improvisational sequences, modal improvising, symmetric/synthetic scale usage, symmetric chord usage, and approach-note/enclosure techniques.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in Jazz Performance or consent of instructor. For Graduate Jazz Performance majors only.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Individ Topics in Music Theory
courses.description: Studies in specialized areas of analysis, theoretical systems, and aesthetics for composition and theory majors and cognates. May be repeated to a maximum of 12 hours.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Graduate Level Composition
courses.description: Advanced instruction in contemporary compositional practice. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 16 hours but no more than 2 hours in any one term, if topics vary.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Sem in Music Comp and Theory
courses.description: Intensive study of selected topics in the fields of music composition and theory. May be repeated.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music composition-theory, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Grad. Jazz Improv. II
courses.description: The advanced application and examination of improvisational methods, device, and techniques. Study of advanced chord/scale relationships, modal harmonic concepts, harmonic analysis, patterns, linear/vertical approaches to improvising, and various jazz song forms including: advanced blues forms, asymmetrical standards, free improvisational forms, and advanced modal forms.
courses.prereqText: MUS 504 or consent of instructor. Graduate Jazz Performance majors only.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Graduate Seminar in Band Conducting, History, and Literature
courses.description: This seminar will explore current topics facing the contemporary wind band conductor. Subject matter will include but not be limited to the exploration of new literature, works for chamber winds, and an historical survey of cornerstone repertoire. There will also be a conducting component, using a chamber ensemble. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours in separate terms, if topics vary.
courses.prereqText: Graduate Band Conducting Majors and Admitted Cognate Program Members Only, or with Instructor permission.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: History of Music Theory
courses.description: The development of theoretical concepts from antiquity through the Renaissance; a study of selected theoretical treatises written before 1550. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in musicology or composition-theory, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Foundations and Methods of Musicology I
courses.description: Introduction to the field for graduate students in musicology and DMA cognates, and graduate minors in Music and Sound Studies. Explores the history and current state of the discipline of historical musicology, introduces methodological approaches, engages critical reading and analysis, and raises topics in professional development. Students will complete an approved research project on a subject of their choice.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in Musicology; DMA cognate in Musicology; Music and Sound Studies graduate minor; or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Fdns/Methods of Musicology II
courses.description: Continues materials introduced in MUS 511. Focuses on the major resources, intellectual history, theories and methodologies of ethnomusicology. Students pursue a state-of-research project on a topic relevant to their interests, selected in consultation with the instructor.
courses.prereqText: MUS 511; Music and Sound Studies graduate minor; or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Topics in Opera History
courses.description: Intensive study of a period or school of opera composition or of a particular aspect of the history of opera. Wide reading in the social and intellectual climate of the period concerned; literary, dramatic, and musical analysis; and work with primary sources, whenever possible. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours if topics vary.
courses.prereqText: MUS 528 A (consult Class Schedule for specific section information); graduate standing in Musicology; Music and Sound Studies graduate minor; or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Musicology and Pedagogy
courses.description: Seminar-style practicum in the teaching of undergraduate courses in Western and non-western music for musicology and non-musicology majors. Intensive review and discussion of pedagogical materials. Instruction in syllabus and lecture design, presentational and discussion styles, and use of multimedia and educational technology.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in Musicology; Music and Sound Studies graduate minor; or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Topics in Vocal Music
courses.description: Intensive or comparative study of specific repertoires of vocal music, of particular genres or styles of vocal composition or performance practice, and/or of particular vocal artists. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: MUS 528 A (consult Class Schedule for specific section information); graduate standing in Musicology; Music and Sound Studies graduate minor; or consent of instructor. Restricted to graduate students.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Fieldwork and Ethnography
courses.description: Prepares students for the various phases of preparing for and doing ethnomusicological fieldwork and ethnographic analysis and writing. Beginning with the project design and grand-writing stages, participants study and practice fieldwork techniques such as participant observations, interviewing, writing and analyzing field notes, and audio and video recording. The politics and ethics of fieldwork and ethnographic writing are considered through readings and discussion. Finally, a variety of approaches to ethnographic writing are considered through the study of finished musical ethnographies.
courses.prereqText: MUS 512; Music and Sound Studies graduate minor; or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Topics in Instrumental Music
courses.description: Intensive or comparative study of specific repertoires of instrumental music, or of particular genres or styles of instrumental composition and performance practice, and/or of particular instrumentalists. Includes broad reading in the social and intellectual climate of the musical practices at issue; pertinent analytical approaches or paradigms; and work with relevant source materials. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: MUS 528 A (consult Class Schedule for specific section information); graduate standing in Musicology; Music and Sound Studies graduate minor; or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Regional Studies in Musicology
courses.description: Seminar devoted to intensive study in the music of specific peoples, states, or geographic regions from around the world. May be repeated to a maximum of 16 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: MUS 528 A (for DMA or MM performance or composition students); graduate standing in Musicology; Music and Sound Studies graduate minor; or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Analytical Methods: Musicology
courses.description: Practical, hands-on experience with and exposure to the transcription, analysis, theoretical constructs, and/or notation of music from any of the world's repertories examined within a musicological framework and from both a synchronic and diachronic perspective. A series of case studies posing an array of technical problems encourage students to think critically about the place of theory and analysis in the history of musicology and their own work. Students repeating should consult with the instructor before enrolling. May be repeated, as topics vary, in the same term to a maximum of 8 hours and in separate terms to a maximum of 12 hours.
courses.prereqText: MUS 511 and MUS 512; or consent of instructor. Graduate students in music will be considered if they passed MUS 528 A (consult Class Schedule for specific section information).

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Social Theory in Ethnomusicology
courses.description: History of theoretical ideas and paradigms that have influenced ethnomusicology from the late 19th century through the early 21st century. Helps students to sharpen their own theoretical tools for conducting ethnomusicological research, teaching, and analysis of existing literature. Participants will study theoretical approaches from anthropology, folkloristics, sociology, semiotics, linguistics, communications, and ethnomusicology that have been influential in ethnomusicology. Participants will write a series of short papers to develop their theoretical thinking, writing, and argumentation.
courses.prereqText: MUS 512; Music and Sound Studies graduate minor; or consent of instructor. Graduate students in Music will be considered if they passed MUS 528 A (consult Class Schedule for specific section information).

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Historical Studies in 20thC Music
courses.description: Seminar in contemporary music, with emphasis on the historical foundations of current trends in musical composition. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: MUS 528 A (consult Class Schedule for specific section information); graduate standing in Musicology; Music and Sound Studies graduate minor; or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Special Topics Seminar
courses.description: Intensive study of special topics in musicology, whether historical, ethnomusicological, or interdisciplinary in approach; seminar format. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: MUS 528 A (consult Class Schedule for specific section information); Music and Sound Studies graduate minor; or consent of instructor. For graduate students in Music; this course is intended for performance and composition majors, especially DMA students seeking advanced musicology credit.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Seminar in Musicology
courses.description: Problems in historical and systematic musicology or ethnomusicology; discussions of special problems and reports on individual research. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in Musicology; Music and Sound Studies graduate minor; or consent of instructor. Graduate students in music will be considered if they passed MUS 528 A (consult Class Schedule for specific section information).

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Seminar in Works of Select Composer
courses.description: Intensive historical and analytical study of the works of important composers; each term devoted to one composer. May be repeated to a maximum of 16 hours.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in Musicology; Music and Sound Studies graduate minor; or consent of instructor. Graduate students in music will be considered if they passed MUS 528 A (consult Class Schedule for specific section information).

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Rdgs in Musicol and Mus Theory
courses.description: Individual guidance in intensive readings in the literature of musicology or music theory, selected in consultation with the instructor and in accordance with the needs and interests of the student. May be repeated. (Summer session, 2 graduate hours).
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in musicology or music theory.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Baroque Performance Practice
courses.description: Study of musical performance from ca. 1600-1750; discussion of musical instruments, ornamentation, basso continuo, etc., supplemented by demonstration performances using the University's collection of instruments.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music; for undergraduates, consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Classical Performance Practice
courses.description: Study of musical performance of the classical period, with an emphasis on the music of Haydn, Mozart, and early Beethoven; discussion of musical instruments, ornamentation, tempo, vibrato, etc., supplemented by demonstration performances using the University's collection of instruments.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music; for undergraduates, consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Res & Bibliography in Music
courses.description: Introduction to basic research skills appropriate to graduate study in music. Topics include accessing library resources and online databases; citation formats and plagiarism issues; critical reading and writing; and critical editions of music. For DMA students additional topics include skills for planning and writing a large research paper; study strategies and resources; and professional skills. All DMA students will complete a draft of their proposal for a final DMA project by the conclusion of this class. Required of all incoming graduate students in the MM (2 hours of credit), except those majoring in musicology, and in the DMA (4 hours of credit).
courses.prereqText: If required, all remedial coursework in ESL and/or music history must be satisfied prior to enrollment.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Transformative Music Education
courses.description: Music educators in all settings operate in a crosscurrent of social, musical, educational, and person values. In order to improve our professional practice and transform the profession, we need to examine society's expectations of schools, education, music and the arts as well as our own. In this course, students will learn how sociology can be used to identify and clarify these connections.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Critical Readings in Mus Ed
courses.description: Independent critical readings and reflections of topics not treated in regularly scheduled courses. Includes program of approved research that culminates in a written report and/or formal presentations. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music education.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Curricular Perspectives on Music Education
courses.description: Examines current issues and trends within music education from both a local and global perspective. Focuses on the status and role of the music curriculum in contemporary schools and includes a critical examination of a range of evidence-based principles and approaches that govern music teaching and learning in formal and informal settings.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music education or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Research in Music Education
courses.description: Examines the sources of research literature in music education, provides an overview of traditional research methodologies, and introduces terminology and procedures utilized in qualitative and quantitative research. The purpose of the course is to enable graduate students to become intelligent consumers and interpreters of the music education research literature.
courses.prereqText: Advanced undergraduate or graduate standing in music or music education, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Doctoral Research in Mus Ed
courses.description: Considers music education research within a wider political and social context and addresses some of the dilemma and choices faced when designing and conducting research. Explores different approaches and considers theoretical and methodological issues relevant to the design and conduct of music education research. Students are expected to design a research project that will make a distinct contribution to knowledge and afford evidence of originality, either by the discovery of new evidence, or by the exercise of independent critical judgments.
courses.prereqText: MUS 533 or equivalent, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Philosophic Inquiry in Mus Ed
courses.description: Consideration of the philosophical assumptions that have guided decisions regarding why, what, and how music is taught in schools. Assists students in placing their present values and beliefs about music learning in the context of scholarly ideas on this subject. Addresses questions such as: What is music? Why do people listen to, create, and perform music? What is music's value for individuals and society? Why teach music in school? How does music fit the large goals of schooling? How have answers to the foregoing changed over the past century?
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music or music education, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music in Higher Education
courses.description: Provides an orientation to the organization, teaching and administration of music in the college or university. Includes topics such as preparing for and securing a college/university faculty position, promotion and tenure, faculty ethics and evaluation, and personnel/personal relations.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music or music education.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Graduate Wind Band Conducting
courses.description: Examination of techniques of rehearsal, conducting, and preparation of wind band and chamber wind ensembles for concert performance. Emphasizes discussion, analysis, and preparation of selected scores for private and group lessons; as well as coaching/experience with live ensembles and select performance opportunities. May be repeated to a maximum of 16 hours.
courses.prereqText: MM wind band conducting students and/or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Chor Prog in Secondary Schools
courses.description: In-depth study of the methods, materials and literature for teaching choral music in the secondary schools. Emphasis on curriculum development, musical literacy, and advanced rehearsal techniques.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music or music education.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music Teacher Education
courses.description: This course focuses on the issues, concepts, and processes for the development of preservice music teachers. Intended for prospective university teachers of undergraduate music education majors. Covers educational philosophy, curriculum design, methods of teaching and evaluation, and student teaching and observational experiences as they relate to undergraduate music teacher programs. 4 graduate hours. No professional hours.
courses.prereqText: PhD Students in Music Education, or as approved by instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Doctoral Seminar in Music Education
courses.description: Weekly seminar involving special topic discussions on critical issues within the profession. Required each semester for all resident doctoral students in music education during their residency.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music education.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Topics in Music Education
courses.description: In-depth study of a topic or issue within music education. May be repeated.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music education.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Orchestral Literature I
courses.description: Study of orchestral and symphonic literature from about 1700 to 1850. May be repeated up to 6 hours,
courses.prereqText: Graduate orchestral conducting majors only; consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Orchestral Literature II
courses.description: Study of orchestral and symphonic literature from about 1850 to the present. May be repeated up to 6 hours.
courses.prereqText: Graduate orchestral conducting majors only; consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Advanced Jazz Harmony I
courses.description: A survey of advanced improvisational theory and its conception, use, and historical lineage. Examines synthetic, symmetric, and asymmetric scales and modes generated from each. Discussion and analysis of chord symbols and their functions in asymmetric song forms. In-class demonstration by students of linear and vertical approaches to improvising on uncommon chord functions.
courses.prereqText: MUS 361, or placement by exam with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Advanced Jazz Harmony II
courses.description: Continuation of materials introduced in MUS 548. Surveys advanced improvisational theory and its conception, use, and historical lineage. Examines use of polychords, pentatonic scales, diminished scales, and the modes generated from each. Discussion and analysis of chord functions in all song forms. Students demonstrate in class a variety of linear and vertical approaches to improvising using harmonic major scales.
courses.prereqText: MUS 548, or placement by exam with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Choral Literature I
courses.description: Survey of choral and vocal ensemble repertoire from the Middle Ages to about 1750.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music; consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Choral Literature II
courses.description: Survey of choral repertoire about 1750 to the present.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music; consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Career Preparation for Opera Singers and Coaches
courses.description: Focuses on the practical side of becoming a professional classical singer. Meetings and coursework consist of mock auditions; student presentations on American (US) opera houses, young artists’ programs, and competitions; the keeping of an audition log; periodic self-evaluations; and discussions with faculty and guests about the structure and nature of our industry. We will discuss the roles that concert work, recitals, digital forms, and musical theatre may play in your career.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to Graduate students in the Music Department; others with instructor approval.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Graduate Orchestral Conducting
courses.description: Study of conducting techniques and problems related to standard orchestral literature. May be repeated to a maximum of 12 hours.
courses.prereqText: MUS 333 or equivalent, and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Opera for Pianists
courses.description: Prepares advanced pianists for success as repetiteurs and assistant conductors in opera houses. Students will be asked to play and sing (as pianists do, not with the vocal qualities of a professional singer) several arias or ensembles each week, which will familiarize them with the most commonly found repertoire in Young Artists Programs in the industry. A working knowledge of French, German, and Italian is assumed. We will discuss prompting, orchestration and reduction, and the role of the rehearsal pianist.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to Graduates in the School of Music; others with instructor permission.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Advanced Choral Conducting
courses.description: Intensive laboratory approach to the development of advanced techniques necessary for working effectively with choral ensembles. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: MM choral conducting students or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Choral Studies
courses.description: Choral Studies is a sequence of four two-credit courses designed to equip the student choral conductor with the skills to lead an efficient rehearsal. The four sections of Choral Studies are Choral Pedagogy, Vocal Pedagogy, Diction and Aural Skills, and Choral Styles Beyond the Canon. May be repeated up to 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in choral music or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Piano Literature
courses.description: May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Vocal Literature
courses.description: Study of solo song in larger works and solo art song. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Organ Literature
courses.description: Intensive study of organ literature from Bach to the present; includes the music itself, recordings, and collateral readings. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: String Instrument Literature
courses.description: May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Wind Instrument Literature
courses.description: Survey of solo and ensemble wind literature; includes analysis and performance (when possible) of the music itself, recordings, and collateral readings. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Percussion Instruments Lit
courses.description: Survey and analysis of the field of solo and ensemble percussion literature; includes analysis and performance (when possible) of the music itself, recordings, and collateral readings. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Topics in Choral Repertoire
courses.description: Critical and analytical study of vocal ensemble and choral music from the Middle Ages to the present. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: MM and DMA in choral conducting students, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Choral Conducting Project
courses.description: Participation in a graduate choral conducting laboratory and preparation of a choral ensemble for public performance. Required during the final term in residence for candidates in the Master of Music in choral music curriculum.
courses.prereqText: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Doctoral Choral Conducting
courses.description: Study of performance problems and musical analysis of choral music with techniques of preparation and rehearsal from the various style periods: Renaissance, Baroque, Classic-Romantic, and Contemporary. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: Admission into the Doctor of Musical Arts choral music program, or the equivalent background in other doctoral programs.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Cripping Music
courses.description: Cripping Music critically and creatively engages the applied research strategies, creative methodologies, and disciplinary conventions of Music via the Crip* principles of interdependence, open access, generative difference, radical alterity, networks of support and collaboration, Crip temporalities, and access ecology. This course will serve to discover and design new crip-centric approaches and strategies specific to Music. Approved for Letter and S/U grading.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Adv Instrument: Chamber/Symph
courses.description: Orchestration for chamber and symphony orchestras; works of Classical, Romantic, and Contemporary composers.
courses.prereqText: Undergraduate course in instrumentation.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Graduate Seminar in Collaborative Piano Techniques
courses.description: Techniques of collaborative piano playing as applied to various stylistic schools and periods of vocal and instrumental duo literature. Includes written and reading assignments as well as in-class presentations, coachings, and performances.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the School of Music.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Capstone Project Synthesis
courses.description: Completion of Master of Music Education curriculum and inquiry capstone project in approved area(s) of study. MME students complete two capstone projects; MME with Licensure students complete one capstone project.
courses.prereqText: MUS 532 and MUS 533.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Prac Pno Tchg Child and Teens
courses.description: Student teaching of group piano and musicianship classes for elementary, middle school, and high school students; weekly seminar devoted to evaluation and improvement of teaching techniques.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Practicum in Piano Tchg Adults
courses.description: Student teaching of group piano for adults in the private studio, community college, and university; weekly seminar devoted to evaluation and improvement of teaching techniques.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing in music or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Doctoral Orchestral Conducting
courses.description: Advanced study in orchestral conducting performance, pedagogy, score study/analysis, and rehearsal techniques. May be repeated to a maximum of 16 hours.
courses.prereqText: Admission into the doctoral concentration in orchestral conducting; consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Doctoral Wind Band Conducting
courses.description: Advanced study in wind band conducting performance, pedagogy, score study/ analysis, and rehearsal techniques. May be repeated to a maximum of 16 hours.
courses.prereqText: Admission into the doctoral concentration in wind band conducting; for doctoral cognate students, consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Jazz Arranging III
courses.description: Advanced arranging styles and orchestration techniques, with emphasis on brass section arranging, saxophone section arranging, and big band arranging. Orchestration techniques with emphasis on band planing (parallelism), 5-part spread, cluster voicings, and line-writing. Study of jazz related re-harmonization techniques with emphasis on tonicization, secondary dominants, and passing chord re-harmonization.
courses.prereqText: MUS 363, or placement by exam/portfolio with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Jazz Arranging IV
courses.description: Continued practice and examination of arranging applications for advanced re-harmonization techniques, including tonicization, secondary dominant re-harmonizations, and passing chord re-harmonizations. Score study of advanced voicing techniques, including 5-part spread, whole and half-step planing (parallelism), and modal line-writing. Advanced notation software is introduced and applied in the classroom. Includes discussion of practical application of jazz arranging in a modern music business context.
courses.prereqText: MUS 574, or placement by exam/portfolio with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Doctoral Projects
courses.description: Special projects for candidates for the Doctor of Musical Arts degree. Open only to students in the Doctor of Musical Arts program. Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated. (Summer session, 0 to 8 graduate hours).
courses.prereqText: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Vocal Pedagogy
courses.description: Explores applications of healthy voice instruction. This class has a flipped and blended learning design in which online work introduces the material and digital tools support training. The classroom is primarily interactive and integrative to address real-world scenarios. May be repeated in separate terms up to 6 hours.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate Music majors.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Accelerated Conducting and Score Study
courses.description: Develops and refines conducting and score study technique. Throughout the semester, students will focus on the merger of the prepared mind and the trained body, gestural specificity, and self-analyzation.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in Music.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Graduate Choral Diction
courses.description: Provides an overview of diction skills for the emerging choral conductor. Using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA), students will learn accurate and fluent pronunciation in the five primary singing languages: Italian, German, French, Latin, and English. In addition, they will develop their ear to recognize and correct pronunciation issues in their own and others' singing. This course is not intended to replace semester-long diction courses for students in the Vocal Performance or Vocal Coaching and Accompanying degrees. Approved for both Letter and S/U grading.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to students enrolled in the MM Choral Music degree.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Thesis Research
courses.description: Research in special projects. Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated in the same term or in separate terms up to a maximum of 16 hours.
courses.prereqText: Consent of instructor.
